## Welcome

Welcome to Signed Instruction Blocks (SIB), a format and a reference implementation for proving
who wrote an instruction to an AI agent, and when.

An agent's permissions today are plain text in a prompt, a file or a chat message, and text can be
written by anyone, including another agent. A signed instruction block keeps the instruction as
readable text and attaches a detached signature from a named human. A verifier in the harness checks
every block in the agent's context on every tool call and emits a provenance manifest that tells the
permission classifier which text is human-signed and which is not. The signature proves authorship;
the classifier resolves meaning; the harness makes the classifier unfoolable about who wrote what.

The block does not encode permissions. Humans write ordinary instructions ("you may deploy to
staging once the tests pass"), and an LLM permission classifier judges whether a proposed action
falls within what a verified human actually said.


## Installation

To get started using the reference implementation:

1. Clone the repository and install the package:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/fastfedora/signed-instructions
   cd signed-instructions
   uv sync
   ```

2. Choose where keys and the registry live, then create and enroll a dev-mode key:

   ```bash
   export SIB_HOME=$PWD/.sib-local
   .venv/bin/sib keygen --kid "alice@example.com#dev-2026-09" --enroll --signer alice@example.com
   ```

3. Sign an instruction and verify it:

   ```bash
   printf 'You may deploy the current main branch to staging with\nscripts/deploy.sh staging whenever the test suite passes.\n' \
     | .venv/bin/sib sign --signer alice@example.com --kid "alice@example.com#dev-2026-09" \
         --expires 8h --audience acme/dev-agent --file - --out block.txt
   .venv/bin/sib verify block.txt --audience acme/dev-agent
   ```

::: {.callout-important}
Phase 1 runs in dev mode: keys are software files, and every signing and verification prints a
warning saying so. A dev-mode signature proves possession of a file, not a person. Biometric
signing with passkeys is Phase 2.
:::


## Getting Started

Once a block verifies on the command line, install the hooks into a project so Claude Code's
permission decision sees the manifest:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m sib.hooks.claude_code.install --project /path/to/repo
```

The installer writes three hooks into the project's `.claude/settings.json` and prints the
`autoMode` rule to add to your user settings. The project also needs a gate policy naming the
audience and the actions that require a signed instruction; see [Claude
Code](guide/integration/claude-code.qmd) for the file and where to keep it.

From then on, every tool call runs the verifier. A gated action with no verified instruction
covering it is denied with a reason that names the nearest unsigned claim. A gated action that a
verified instruction covers proceeds, and the manifest cites the block it relied on.
